title: Jeremiah Chapter 31 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 31 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 31 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 31.

questions.question: Who will be the God of all the families of Israel according to Jeremiah 31?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD will be the God of all the families of Israel (Jeremiah 31:1).

questions.question: What did the people who were left of the sword find in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that the people found grace in the wilderness (Jeremiah 31:2).

questions.question: True or False: The LORD loves with a fleeting love.
questions.explanation: The LORD loves with an everlasting love, as stated in Jeremiah 31:3.

questions.question: What will happen to Israel again according to Jeremiah 31?
questions.explanation: The LORD promises to build Israel again (Jeremiah 31:4).

questions.question: What will the planters do on the mountains of Samaria?
questions.explanation: The verse states that they shall plant vines upon the mountains of Samaria (Jeremiah 31:5).

questions.question: True or False: The watchmen upon mount Ephraim will encourage people to go up to Zion.
questions.explanation: The watchmen will cry to arise and go up to Zion (Jeremiah 31:6).

questions.question: According to the LORD, what should the people do for Jacob?
questions.explanation: The verse instructs to sing with gladness for Jacob (Jeremiah 31:7).

questions.question: What will the LORD gather from the north country?
questions.explanation: The LORD will gather a great company of people (Jeremiah 31:8).

questions.question: True or False: Ephraim is referred to as the firstborn of Israel.
questions.explanation: Ephraim is called the firstborn in Jeremiah 31:9.

questions.question: What shall be like a watered garden according to the passage?
questions.explanation: The people shall be as a watered garden (Jeremiah 31:12).

questions.question: In Jeremiah 31, who will turn mourning into joy?
questions.explanation: The LORD promises to turn their mourning into joy (Jeremiah 31:13).

questions.question: What will happen to the children of Israel according to Jeremiah 31:17?
options: They shall come again to their own border
questions.correctAnswer: They shall come again to their own border
questions.explanation: The verse states that the children shall come again to their own border (Jeremiah 31:17).

questions.question: True or False: The LORD will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the LORD will make a new covenant (Jeremiah 31:31).

questions.question: In Jeremiah 31, what is said to be written in the hearts of the people?
questions.explanation: The covenant states that the LORD will put His law in their inward parts and write it in their hearts (Jeremiah 31:33).

questions.question: What will not be remembered anymore by the LORD?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD will forgive their iniquity and will remember their sin no more (Jeremiah 31:34).

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 31 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 31 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does the LORD promise to do for the families of Israel?
questions.explanation: The LORD declares that He will be the God of all the families of Israel in Jeremiah 31:1, establishing a personal relationship with them.

questions.question: According to the LORD, who found grace in the wilderness?
options: The people which were left of the sword
questions.correctAnswer: The people which were left of the sword
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:2 mentions that the people which were left of the sword found grace in the wilderness, indicating God's mercy.

questions.question: What will the people of Israel do again, according to Jeremiah 31:4?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 31:4, the LORD promises that Israel, referred to as a virgin, will again be adorned and go forth in dances, signifying joy.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 31:9 suggest about God's guidance?
options: He will lead them with a strong hand
He will cause them to walk by rivers of water
He will send them to the mountains
He will shelter them in caves
questions.correctAnswer: He will cause them to walk by rivers of water
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:9 reveals that God leads His people with care, causing them to walk by the rivers in a straight way, illustrating His guidance.

questions.question: What does the LORD say will happen to Ephraim according to Jeremiah 31:20?
options: He will have mercy upon him
questions.correctAnswer: He will have mercy upon him
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 31:20, the LORD expresses His troubled feelings for Ephraim and promises to have mercy upon him, showing His compassion.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 31:25 describe God's provision?
options: He will satiate the weary soul
He will take away their joy
questions.correctAnswer: He will satiate the weary soul
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:25 indicates that God provides comfort and replenishment for the weary and sorrowful, demonstrating His care.

questions.question: What significant promise is made in Jeremiah 31:31?
options: A new covenant will be made
questions.correctAnswer: A new covenant will be made
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:31 introduces the promise of a new covenant with the house of Israel and Judah, which signifies a new relationship with God.

questions.question: What does the new covenant entail according to Jeremiah 31:33?
options: The law will be written on tablets
The law will be put in their inward parts
The law will be the same as before
questions.correctAnswer: The law will be put in their inward parts
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:33 states that God will write His law in the hearts of His people, indicating a deeper, internalized relationship.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 31:34, what will no longer be necessary?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:34 mentions that they shall teach no more every man his neighbor to know the LORD, for all will know Him directly, indicating a transformation in relationship.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promises that Ephraim has no hope for the future.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:17 assures that there is hope for Ephraim, stating that his children shall return to their own border, indicating a restoration.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD will forget the sins of His people according to Jeremiah 31:34.
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 31:34, the LORD promises to forgive their iniquity and remember their sin no more, which signifies complete forgiveness.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD states that every man will die for his own iniquity in Jeremiah 31:30.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:30 clearly states that every man shall die for his own iniquity, emphasizing personal responsibility for sin.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 31:27 imply about the future of Israel and Judah?
options: They will be replanted and cared for
questions.correctAnswer: They will be replanted and cared for
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:27 states that the LORD will sow the house of Israel and Judah, indicating His intention to restore and care for them.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 31:28 say about God's oversight of His people?
options: He will watch over them to build and plant
questions.correctAnswer: He will watch over them to build and plant
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:28 emphasizes God's commitment to watch over His people to build and plant, demonstrating His protective and nurturing nature.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 31 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 31.

questions.question: What does the LORD promise regarding the families of Israel in Jeremiah 31?
options: He will give them new leaders
questions.explanation: The LORD states, 'I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people' (Jeremiah 31:1).

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 31:3, how does the LORD express His love for Israel?
questions.explanation: The LORD says, 'I have loved thee with an everlasting love' (Jeremiah 31:3), indicating His enduring affection for Israel.

questions.question: What will the watchmen on Mount Ephraim proclaim according to Jeremiah 31:6?
options: Let us go up to Zion
questions.correctAnswer: Let us go up to Zion
questions.explanation: The watchmen will cry, 'Arise ye, and let us go up to Zion unto the LORD our God' (Jeremiah 31:6).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 31:11 say about the fate of Jacob?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For the LORD hath redeemed Jacob' (Jeremiah 31:11), highlighting God's act of redemption.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 31:34, what promise does the LORD make about knowing Him?
options: They will teach each other about Him
Only the leaders will know Him
He will be unknown to them
questions.explanation: The LORD declares, 'for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them' (Jeremiah 31:34).

questions.question: Which concept does Jeremiah 31:32 contrast with the new covenant?
options: The covenant made with their fathers
questions.correctAnswer: The covenant made with their fathers
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts the new covenant with 'the covenant that I made with their fathers' (Jeremiah 31:32).

questions.question: What does the phrase 'sour grape' in Jeremiah 31:29 symbolize?
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that individuals will not suffer for the sins of their ancestors but will face their own iniquities (Jeremiah 31:29).

questions.question: How is the new covenant described in Jeremiah 31:33?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts' (Jeremiah 31:33).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 31:35 refer to when mentioning the ordinances of the sun and moon?
questions.explanation: The verse illustrates God's sovereignty over creation, stating that He gives light by day and night (Jeremiah 31:35).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 31:37 suggest about God's commitment to Israel?
options: He will cast them off forever
questions.explanation: The LORD states, 'If heaven above can be measured...I will also cast off all the seed of Israel' (Jeremiah 31:37), emphasizing His unwavering commitment.

questions.question: True or False: The new covenant mentioned in Jeremiah 31:31 is similar to the covenant made with the fathers.
questions.explanation: The new covenant is explicitly stated to be 'not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers' (Jeremiah 31:32).

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 31:40 indicates that the valley of dead bodies will be holy unto the LORD.
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'shall be holy unto the LORD' (Jeremiah 31:40), indicating a future sanctification of that area.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Jeremiah 31 to highlight God's plans for Israel?
questions.explanation: The structure of the promises and judgments in this chapter forms a chiasm, emphasizing the balance of God's justice and mercy.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with the theme of the new covenant in Jeremiah 31:31?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 26:28, Jesus refers to the 'new covenant in my blood,' connecting directly to Jeremiah's prophecy about the new covenant.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 31 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 31 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 31:1 reveal about God's relationship with Israel?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:1 states, 'At the same time, saith the LORD, will I be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people.' This verse emphasizes God's commitment to His covenant relationship with Israel.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'I have loved thee with an everlasting love' in Jeremiah 31:3?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 31:3, 'Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love,' indicates the nature of God's love for Israel, which is eternal and unwavering, showcasing His faithfulness.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 31:13, what transformation does the Lord promise to bring?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:13 states, 'for I will turn their mourning into joy,' which highlights God's promise to restore joy to His people, indicating His redemptive work.

questions.question: What does God promise in Jeremiah 31:34 regarding knowledge of Him?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:34 says, 'for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them,' indicating a future intimate relationship between God and His people where personal knowledge of Him will be universal.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 31:11 indicate about God's action towards Jacob?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 31:11, it states, 'For the LORD hath redeemed Jacob,' showcasing God's redemptive nature, emphasizing His role as a savior.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 31:22 refer to regarding a new creation?
options: A man shall compass a woman
A woman shall compass a man
questions.correctAnswer: A woman shall compass a man
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:22 states, 'A woman shall compass a man,' which signifies a new role in relationships and potentially foreshadows a redemptive reversal of roles in God's plan.

questions.question: What does the gathering of Israel in Jeremiah 31:8 symbolize?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:8, which speaks of bringing back 'the blind and the lame,' symbolizes God's promise of restoration and the return of His people from exile.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 31:17, what is the nature of the hope that is described?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:17 states, 'that thy children shall come again to their own border,' highlighting the hope of restoration and reunion for the people of Israel.

questions.question: What is affirmed about God's mercy in Jeremiah 31:20?
options: He will have mercy upon Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: He will have mercy upon Ephraim
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:20 declares, 'I will surely have mercy upon him,' reaffirming God's compassionate nature and commitment to His people despite their failings.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 31:36 imply about God's faithfulness to Israel?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:36 emphasizes, 'If those ordinances depart from before me... then the seed of Israel also shall cease,' indicating that God's promises to Israel are irrevocable.

questions.question: What does the new covenant in Jeremiah 31:31 signify?
options: A continuation of the old covenant
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:31 states, 'I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel,' which signifies a new and transformative relationship between God and His people, distinct from the former covenant.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 31:28 reflect God's sovereign oversight?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 31:28, 'so will I watch over them, to build, and to plant,' reflects God's sovereign oversight and intention to restore and bless His people.

questions.question: What does the lamentation in Jeremiah 31:15 symbolize?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:15 describes 'lamentation, and bitter weeping,' which symbolizes the deep sorrow and despair of loss experienced by the people of Israel during their exile.

questions.question: What sceptics claim about God's promises to Israel is addressed in Jeremiah 31:37?
questions.explanation: Sceptics claim that God has abandoned His promises to Israel. Jeremiah 31:37 asserts, 'I will also cast off all the seed of Israel for all that they have done,' affirming that God's promises remain eternal and unbroken.

questions.question: What does the imagery of planting in Jeremiah 31:27 reflect about God's intentions?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:27, 'I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah,' reflects God's intentions for rebirth and growth, indicating a new beginning for His people.
